name: Jeziel
overview: Jeziel was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Azmaveth. He is noted in Scripture for coming to David at Ziklag, indicating his allegiance during a critical period of David's rise to kingship. His presence among those who joined David reflects his role within the unfolding biblical narrative of Israel's monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeziel appears once in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin provided. It is presented simply as a proper name, with no additional titles or meanings indicated in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Jeziel was the son of Azmaveth, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Jeziel's significance lies in his association with David during the time at Ziklag, a pivotal moment when David was gathering support from various tribes. As a Benjaminite and son of Azmaveth, his joining David underscores the unifying movement around David's leadership and the consolidation of support from Israel's tribes. Though not extensively detailed, his mention highlights the individuals who contributed to the establishment of David's kingdom.
